subsystems.name: Disk body
subsystems.role: the plate itself — so massive that its own gravity, not rotation, supplies weight on the surface.

subsystems.name: Central aperture and star
subsystems.role: a hole at the middle through which a star repeatedly passes, lighting first one face then the other.

subsystems.name: Habitable surface
subsystems.role: the terraced top face where people would live.

subsystems.name: Atmosphere retention
subsystems.role: holds air against the pull of the disk's own edge.

subsystems.name: Structural stabilisation
subsystems.role: prevents the slab from buckling out of plane under its own gravity.

subsystems.name: Gravity and tidal management
subsystems.role: the shape of the mass distribution sets surface gravity and the strength of tides across the disk.

subsystems.name: Energy and industry
subsystems.role: supplies the power and materials to keep the surface habitable and the structure maintained.

buildSteps.title: Gather the material
buildSteps.detail: A disk providing 1 g by its own mass is thousands of times the mass of a planet — the raw material would have to be stripped from many star systems, not one.

buildSteps.title: Site and shape the slab
buildSteps.detail: A thick annular plate is formed with an inner radius of roughly an astronomical unit, tapering in thickness so surface gravity is even.

buildSteps.title: Establish internal support
buildSteps.detail: Ribs, vaults and load paths carry the weight of the surface, since no known material can span these distances without sagging.

buildSteps.title: Cut and reinforce the aperture
buildSteps.detail: The central hole is formed last and ringed with the strongest structure, because it concentrates the greatest stresses.

buildSteps.title: Add active stabilisation
buildSteps.detail: Because gravity will tend to pull the flat disk into a lump, continuous active correction is needed to keep it planar.

buildSteps.title: Build rim walls and add air
buildSteps.detail: Walls tens of kilometres tall would be needed to stop the atmosphere spilling over the edge; then an atmosphere is introduced.

buildSteps.title: Capture the star
buildSteps.detail: A star is steered into a periodic path through the aperture, so that each face gets a day and a night.

buildSteps.title: Terraform the face
buildSteps.detail: Only after structure, light and air are settled could soil, water and ecosystems be established.

prerequisites.tech: Structural material of extreme strength-to-mass ratio
prerequisites.why: the shell would have to span millions of kilometres without collapsing; no known or projected material comes close.
building and moving masses larger than planets is far beyond present capability.
a thin, flat disk of planetary mass is unstable and would fold up on itself.
the design depends on a star shuttling through the central hole in a controlled cycle.
an unenclosed surface of this size cannot hold air, even with very tall rim walls.

pathway.milestone: the concept exists only on paper, in 1970s speculative engineering writing
pathway.unlocks: a benchmark for thinking about how large a habitable surface gravity alone allows.

pathway.milestone: large in-space manufacturing and asteroid-scale construction
pathway.unlocks: the industrial base any megastructure would start from.

pathway.milestone: planet-scale structures and controlled gravity engineering
pathway.unlocks: proof that a body's own mass can be shaped into a stable, habitable surface.

pathway.milestone: stellar engineering — moving or capturing stars
pathway.unlocks: the illumination cycle the design needs, and the material from which it could be built.
